problems.title: The stopping heuristic is not a signed trajectory increment
problems.source_location: Section 3.3–3.4, PDF p.5; verifier.py, lines 69–97; inference.py, lines 962–1005
claim: The paper sums observed planning/action log-probability ratios and stops when their signed increment is below a positive threshold; source uses a change norm of next-token vocabulary log-ratio vectors.
analysis: At observed token \(0\), scale \(1\), threshold \(0.5\), distributions \((0.2,0.8)\) versus \((0.8,0.2)\) give signed increment \(-\log4<0.5\), but vector change from zero has norm \(\sqrt2\log4>0.5\). Conversely, repeating ratio vector \((\log4,-\log4)\) across states gives norm \(0\) but a positive new token increment \(\log4>0.5\). Source slices only the final input-logit row, which predicts a future token, instead of gathering preceding rows for observed events. For three observed ratios \(9\) and an equal final distribution, the required sum is \(3\log9\), but the retained vector is zero.
result: Both event choice and aggregation differ. The threshold requests TerminateAction; actual loop exit depends on the returned action, and a separate ten-iteration cap remains. These examples do not satisfy every theorem premise and do not refute its abstract stopping theorem.
repair: Teacher-force and causally align actual newly scored planning/action tokens, gather their log probabilities and sum signed ratios with an explicit mask. Exclude prompt/tool/padding/previously counted content; complete multimodal integration and threshold calibration remain unverified. Alternatively define and analyze the distinct heuristic.

problems.title: BLINK accuracy silently conditions on successful execution
claim: Exception cases are logged without an answer record, while accuracy divides by stored answers and labels that count dataset length.
analysis: For two valid planned examples, one correct response and one inference exception produce \(1/1=100\%\) from the source flow. Planned-set accuracy with failure unsuccessful is \(1/2=50\%\), and coverage is \(50\%\). The exception may concern a valid image/question; malformed labels are unnecessary. When every inference succeeds the two denominators agree.
result: The release reports success-conditional accuracy for failed runs. No historical failure count or corrected benchmark value is established.
repair: Retain an explicit status for every planned ID and report coverage/failures with the predefined scoring/retry policy. Do not silently remove failed predictions from a full-benchmark denominator.

problems.title: The MathVista ablation configurations need reconciliation
problems.source_location: Main Table 2, PDF p.9; Appendix L/Table 10, PDF p.38
claim: Apparently corresponding Qwen2.5VL rows report MathVista \(52.60,66.50\) versus \(7.80,23.52\); Qwen2VL rows report \(37.50,60.30\) versus \(20.24,23.80\).
analysis: The V*Bench/MMStar columns match for the four rows, supporting a configuration comparison, but not proving MathVista protocols coincide. Main full-minus-counterpart gains are \(13.90,22.80\), versus appendix \(15.72,3.56\). Different splits, checkpoints, answer extraction or denominators could explain the values; neither table is automatically the correction. The BLINK accounting defect does not establish a MathVista cause.
result: Unresolved candidate result/protocol inconsistency; raw experiment identity is needed before a numerical error is adjudicated.
